item.title: New Java Library for Qdrant Vector Search Engine Released
item.description:
New Java Library for Qdrant Vector Search Engine Released

A new Java library for the Qdrant vector search engine has been released, providing a high-level client with utility methods for interfacing with Qdrant. The library requires Java 8 or above and uses a low-level gRPC client internally to interact with Qdrant.

📦 Installation

To install the library, add the following lines to your build config file. Please ensure all necessary dependencies listed in the documentation are included in your project.

🛠️ How It Works

The client provides convenient methods and overloads for common operations, including:

  • Creating a new collection
  • Inserting vectors into a collection
  • Searching for similar vectors
  • Searching for similar vectors with filtering conditions

🔐 Configuration

Additional constructor overloads allow fine-grained control over the gRPC client configuration. For example, the following demonstrates how to configure a client to use TLS with certificate validation via the root CA and API key authentication.

🔄 Lifecycle Management

The client implements AutoCloseable, though it is typically created once and used for the application’s lifetime. When constructed by passing a ManagedChannel, the client does not shut down the channel on close by default. It can be configured to shut down the channel upon closing instead.

⏱️ Asynchronous Operations

All client methods return ListenableFuture<T>, enabling asynchronous workflows.

📚 Resources

Usage examples are available in the Qdrant documentation and API Reference.

#Java #Qdrant #VectorSearch #gRPC #ArtificialIntelligence

Source: qdrant/java-client

item.title: Microsoft publishes open-source Model Context Protocol curriculum and Qdrant memory server
item.description:
Microsoft publishes open-source Model Context Protocol curriculum and Qdrant memory server

Microsoft has released an open-source curriculum for the Model Context Protocol (MCP) alongside an official MCP server for Qdrant, enabling developers to build modular, secure AI workflows and implement semantic memory layers using specific language examples and vector search integration.

🧩 The MCP Curriculum

The new open-source curriculum introduces the fundamentals of MCP through real-world, cross-language examples. It is designed for developers to learn practical techniques for building modular, scalable, and secure AI workflows, covering everything from session setup to service orchestration.

  • Languages Covered: C#, Java, JavaScript, Rust, Python, and TypeScript.
  • Repository: The resources are hosted at https://github.com/microsoft/mcp-for-beginners.git.
  • Global Accessibility: The repository includes more than 50 language translations. Note that these translations significantly increase the download size.
  • Community Support: Developers can join the Microsoft Foundry Discord community using the provided link.

🧠 The Qdrant MCP Server

The release includes an official Model Context Protocol server for keeping and retrieving memories in the Qdrant vector search engine. This server acts as a semantic memory layer on top of the Qdrant database and is based on FastMCP.

Core Tools

  • qdrant-store: Stores information in the Qdrant database.
  • qdrant-find: Retrieves relevant information from the Qdrant database.

Configuration Details

Configuration is handled via environment variables, and the only command-line argument is --transport, which selects the transport protocol. You cannot provide both QDRANT_URL and QDRANT_LOCAL_PATH simultaneously.

Environment Variable Description
QDRANT_LOCAL_PATH Path to the local Qdrant database (alternative to QDRANT_URL)
EMBEDDING_PROVIDER Embedding provider to use (currently only “fastembed” is supported)
EMBEDDING_MODEL Name of the embedding model to use
QDRANT_SEARCH_LIMIT Maximum number of results to return from search
QDRANT_READ_ONLY Enable read-only mode (disables qdrant-store tool)
FASTMCP_HOST Host address to bind the server to (SSE and HTTP transports)
FASTMCP_PORT Port to run the server on (SSE and HTTP transports)
FASTMCP_MASK_ERROR_DETAILS Hide exception details from tool error messages sent to clients

Naming Conventions

Before version 0.9.0, settings used the FASTMCP_SERVER_ prefix (e.g., FASTMCP_SERVER_HOST). The old names FASTMCP_SERVER_HOST, FASTMCP_SERVER_PORT, and FASTMCP_SERVER_DEBUG still work but are deprecated and will be removed in a future release. If both old and new names are set, the new name takes precedence.

🚀 Availability and Usage

The mcp-server-qdrant can be run directly without specific installation steps by using uvx. The server supports different transport protocols specified using the --transport flag.

#MCP #Microsoft #Qdrant #AIDevelopment #OpenSource

Source: microsoft/mcp-for-beginners Source: qdrant/mcp-server-qdrant

item.title: Go client released for Qdrant vector search engine
item.description:
Go client released for Qdrant vector search engine

The Go client for the Qdrant vector search engine has been released, making it easier for developers to integrate vector search capabilities into their Go applications. Internally, the high-level client uses a low-level gRPC client to interact with Qdrant, abstracting away the complexity of direct API calls. The client supports secure communication with TLS 1.3 as the minimum required version when UseTLS is enabled.

📦 Availability

The client can be installed using the Go package manager:

  • go get -u github.com/qdrant/go-client

🔐 Security

  • Uses TLS 1.3 as the minimum security version when UseTLS: true is set

🧩 Architecture

  • High-level client provides simplified API for common operations
  • Low-level gRPC client handles direct communication with Qdrant server

💡 Why it matters

This release enables Go developers to leverage Qdrant’s vector search capabilities without implementing low-level networking code, accelerating the development of AI and machine learning applications that require semantic search functionality.

#Go #Qdrant #VectorSearch #gRPC #TLS #AI

Source: qdrant/go-client

item.title: Qdrant Vector Search Tutorial Collection Released
item.description:
Qdrant Vector Search Tutorial Collection Released

A new collection of examples and tutorials has been released for the Qdrant vector search engine. The repository contains a curated set of tutorials, demos, and how-to guides focused on Qdrant and adjacent technologies.

🧩 How it works

The tutorials cover a range of data types and use cases, including:

  • Text Data: Introduction to the intersection of vector databases and natural language processing.
  • Image Data: Use of semantic search for accurate skin cancer image comparison with Qdrant and CLIP.
  • Audio Data: Introduction to audio embeddings, audio data, and music recommendation systems.
  • Agentic RAG: Building a vector-search-powered agentic workflow to extract insights from meeting recordings using Qdrant and CrewAI.

⚙️ Key details

Specific guides within the collection include:

  • “Qdrant 101 - Getting Started”: Introduction to semantic search and the recommendation API of Qdrant.
  • “Build a Semantic Search Engine in 5 Minutes”: A quick starter tutorial that builds a semantic search engine for science-fiction books.
  • “Semantic Search for Sci-Fi Books”: A demonstration of semantic search over a top-100 set of science-fiction books.
  • “Build a Semantic Search API”: A guide to searching startup descriptions by meaning with Qdrant Cloud Inference, filtering by city, and serving results through FastAPI.
  • “Language Model QA with Qdrant”: A tutorial on document retrieval with Vision Language Models and binary quantization.
  • “AI Getting Started Demo”: A sample menu dataset and pre-written script used by the “Start building on Qdrant” agent prompt in the Qdrant docs to demo local semantic search.

💡 Why it matters

The collection provides structured learning paths for developers, covering foundational concepts such as the recommendation API and advanced implementations like agentic workflows and visual document retrieval.

#Qdrant #VectorSearch #SemanticSearch #RAG #Tutorials #CLIP

Source: qdrant/examples

item.title: Qdrant Helm Chart Enables Kubernetes Deployment with Community Support
item.description:
Qdrant Helm Chart Enables Kubernetes Deployment with Community Support

The Qdrant Helm chart has been introduced, enabling users to deploy Qdrant within their Kubernetes clusters. While distributed deployment is possible, the chart lacks advanced features found in Qdrant Cloud and Private Cloud Enterprise Operator offerings.

📦 Deployment Options

The Helm chart is classified as open-source and provides a quick start for local or development environments. It installs the latest version of Qdrant by default.

🔧 Upgrade Process

Users can perform rolling upgrades using standard Helm commands:

1
2

helm repo update
helm upgrade your-qdrant-installation-name qdrant/qdrant

When a new Qdrant version is released, this procedure updates one node at a time. Any custom image tag overrides in values.yaml must be updated before executing the upgrade.

⚖️ Feature Comparison

A feature comparison table highlights differences between the Helm chart and Qdrant Cloud:

Feature Helm Chart Qdrant Cloud
Zero-downtime upgrades Limited Full support
Monitoring, logging Basic Advanced
Backup and disaster recovery Not included Included
Enterprise support Community only Available

Additional Qdrant Cloud capabilities include API keys with granular access control, data loss prevention on downscaling, automatic shard rebalancing, and full cluster backup functionality.

📚 Resources

For detailed configuration guidance, consult the helm chart’s README. Information about Qdrant Cloud deployment options is available at Qdrant Cloud.

#Kubernetes #Qdrant #Helm #AI

Source: qdrant/qdrant-helm
